cards.subject: Français
cards.name: Mémoriser et réemployer le vocabulaire
cards.description: Understand the French word forms and meanings in taught familiar-topic vocabulary sets, retain them beyond immediate repetition, and independently use them appropriately in French conversation or play.
evidence: Identify the meaning of taught French nouns, actions and feeling words in a familiar spoken message or scene, rather than infer success from English vocabulary.
Retrieve the French word forms after a delay and use them appropriately without an immediate spoken model.
Use taught French vocabulary independently in a different familiar scene or exchange, showing meaning as well as a memorized sound sequence.
cards.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} learns a small set of French words for objects, actions and feelings, can they identify their meanings in a new French message, then a few days later independently use the French words appropriately in another familiar scene or conversation rather than only echoing a model?

cards.subject: Français
cards.name: Articuler les consonnes
cards.description: Produce intelligible French consonant contrasts, including t/k, f/v, s/z, p/b, t/d, k/g and ch compared with s/j/z, and retain consonants in clusters such as br, cr, bl and pl in words and short phrases. Judge meaningful contrasts using a qualified model of the intended French variety, without treating a legitimate accent difference as an error.
evidence: Produce French words that preserve the intended t/k, f/v, s/z, p/b, t/d and k/g contrasts, using familiar meaningful examples.
Keep French ch distinct from s, j and z where those are distinct in the target variety; make the intended word intelligible in a phrase.
Produce br, cr, bl and pl clusters without dropping a consonant, and transfer the operation to another familiar word rather than only echo a practiced list.
cards.assessmentPrompt: Using familiar French words and a qualified French model, can {{name}} say contrasting words such as poule/boule and chou/sou distinctly and keep the consonants in bras, crabe, bleu and pluie? Can a listener distinguish the intended words in a short phrase and in another familiar word carrying the same contrast, without relying only on immediate repetition?

cards.subject: Français
cards.name: Distinguer les voyelles nasales
cards.description: Hear and produce the French oral/nasal vowel distinctions and contrasts among nasal vowels used in the intended French variety. Use meaningful familiar words and respect regional phonetic variation, including whether the in/un contrast is maintained; do not assume that every French variety has only three nasal vowels.
evidence: Identify which familiar word a speaker says in oral/nasal contrast examples, using meaning or pictures so a spoken French answer is not required to demonstrate listening.
Produce familiar words with oral versus nasal vowels intelligibly and preserve the nasal-vowel contrasts of the target variety, including in/un where distinct.
Recognize and produce the same contrasts in another voice or familiar word/phrase without merely copying the immediately preceding model.
cards.assessmentPrompt: With familiar French words and a qualified model of the intended variety, can {{name}} hear which word is said in contrasts such as bas/banc, beau/bon and paix/pain, then produce the words distinctly in a short phrase? Include brun/brin when the target variety distinguishes un/in, and check transfer with another voice or familiar word rather than marking a legitimate regional merger wrong.

assessmentProtocols.materials: Teacher-selected familiar French corpus with nouns, actions and feeling words, pictures/scenes, varied short French messages and a qualified fluent French model. The corpus and intended meanings are explicit; no claim of all-French vocabulary mastery.
task: Check meaning by selecting/acting out the intended referent in varied spoken French sentences; an English explanation or pointing can isolate comprehension from production.
After a few days without an immediate spoken model, ask for independent appropriate French words in another familiar scene or exchange.
Check recombination and retained meaning, not only an immediate correct echo.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Recognizes taught French meanings in a new utterance and later independently retrieves appropriate French forms.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Repeats a sound once or supplies only the English word; fails meaning selection or later independent French retrieval.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: Another familiar context and speaker, with taught forms recombined.

assessmentProtocols.materials: Qualified French model and familiar meaningful words covering the card’s specified contrasts and clusters. Teach unfamiliar word meanings first; hearing/clinical motor diagnosis is not inferred.
task: Elicit the contrasted French words and clusters in short phrases, not only an isolated immediate imitation.
Use another familiar word carrying each taught contrast/cluster and ask an informed listener to identify the intended word.
Respect the intended variety’s legitimate pronunciation; evaluate meaningful intelligibility, not resemblance to one accent.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Intelligible intended contrasts and clusters in words and short connected phrases, retained in transfer.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Neutralizes a required contrast or drops a cluster consonant so the intended word cannot be distinguished.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: Different familiar words/phrase and listener while preserving the same phonological operation.

assessmentProtocols.materials: Qualified model of the chosen French variety; meaning/picture cards and recordings or live utterances from more than one voice. OQLF describes four nasal vowels in its Quebec model and different Quebec/European transcriptions; do not impose a universal three-vowel inventory.
task: Check listening identification of oral/nasal contrasts separately from speaking, allowing pointing or an English response.
Check production in meaningful familiar words and phrases, using bas/banc, beau/bon and paix/pain as varied lexical contrasts, not as a claim that each pair differs only in nasalization.
Include the in/un distinction where maintained by the chosen variety; accept a legitimate regional merger and document the model rather than infer a deficit.
Use another voice and familiar word to check transfer beyond echoing.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Recognizes and produces the intended variety’s meaningful oral/nasal and nasal-vowel contrasts.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Relies on a memorized immediate echo without hearing the meaning distinction, or neutralizes a contrast that is required in the chosen variety.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: Another voice and familiar lexical context, with comprehension and production scored separately.

records.requirementSummary: Understand varied familiar oral French texts
remainingConditions: Variety of oral genres/purposes and meaning beyond a taught vocabulary set, plus appropriate listening strategies, remain explicit.
General listening strategies require a complete cross-language reuse review and actual French application; no strategy clone is adopted here.

records.requirementSummary: Understand familiar everyday French messages with support
remainingConditions: Lexical meaning and phonological listening contribute; message purpose, connected meaning and varied texts need a source-fit listening dossier.

records.requirementSummary: Produce oral French for purpose and audience
remainingConditions: A coherent French message with suitable strategy, purpose/audience and connected form is broader than vocabulary and sound components.

records.requirementSummary: Use strategies for coherent purposeful French speech
remainingConditions: Audience/coherence strategies require reuse review plus actual French formulation; generic English success is insufficient.

records.requirementSummary: Produce brief rehearsed familiar French messages
remainingConditions: Vocabulary retrieval contributes, while meaningful connected messages about familiar topics and appropriate supports remain an integrated task.
Consonants and nasal vowels contribute; pace, intonation and connected-message intelligibility beyond selected contrasts remain required.

consumerBoundary: No mastery transfer from English or FrenchL1, no crosswalk-driven learner-state update. New stable IDs are independently assessed. Adoption does not accept the rest of PR23 or publish to a DB.

retainedCandidates.boundary: Few-minute spoken message, ordering/global meaning/monitoring; greetings alone do not satisfy whole claim.
Independent prepared connected talk with organizers; not adult-led isolated frames.
All-person present être/avoir in speech and writing; je suis/j’ai alone is insufficient.

checkpointMeaning: The seven Partial dispositions below describe the initial pilot only. Current seven-record authoring dispositions are in currentReport; this remains the original three-card attribution/semantic checkpoint.
